newsitem.title: USA: Fed's Rivlin urges Congress act on bank powers.
newsitem.headline: Fed's Rivlin urges Congress act on bank powers.

text.p: Regulators have done what they can to expand bank powers within existing law and it is now vital for lawmakers to do their part to bolster the financial system, Federal Reserve Vice-Chairman Alice Rivlin said Thursday.

"Artificial barriers between and among various forms of financial activity are harmful to the best interests of the consumers of financial services, to the providers of those services and to the general stability and well-being of our financial system," Rivlin told a forum on banking issues sponsored by the Brookings Institution.
A text of her remarks was released in advance of delivery.

Rivlin noted that reform efforts to break down existing barriers in the Depression-era Glass-Steagall Act against banks participating in many financial activities have foundered in several past Congresses.
"We are hopeful that the 105th Congress will succeed where its predecessors have failed," she said, since there is little more regulators can do until the laws are changed.
"While the regulators can move in the right direction, it is still imperative that Congress act," Rivlin said, "Congress should consider this issue and take the next steps."

Rivlin said the Fed has proposed liberalization of a number of activities to permit broadened participation by banks and that the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency has taken steps to liberalize banks' insurance agency powers.
She noted the Fed believes some of the broadened activities should be carried out by a subsidiary of the holding company rather than a bank subsidiary.

"We believe that the more distance between the bank and its new, nonbank operations, the more likely that we can separate one from the other" and avoid risks from one activity affecting other operations.
